channel.title: North Wales Chronicle - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from North Wales Chronicle (northwaleschronicle.co.uk)

item.title: Students from North Wales shaping government reform on online safety
item.description: Young people are helping shape national policy on online safety.

item.title: Footpath near the Britannia Bridge closed to allow for repairs
item.description: A footpath in Pentir is closed due to cable fault repairs.

item.title: Holyhead transport company in administration ordered to pay 80 employees
item.description: A Holyhead-based transport company which went into administration two years ago has been ordered to issue payouts to 80 of its former employees.

item.title: North Wales teenager who lost friends to suicide criticises mental health services
item.description: Lucy Hughes, 17, says long waits, inconsistent support and a system “not ready” for the scale of young people’s needs are leaving vulnerable teenagers “in limbo” - the health board has apologised and says work is under way to improve access.

item.title: LOOK: Aftermath of blaze that caused major damage to Anglesey home
item.description: A property on Anglesey sustained "significant smoke damage" following a fire, as the fire service warned residents of the dangers of deep frying food at home.

item.title: Conwy Tunnel set for six nights of closures with contraflow in place
item.description: The A55 Conwy Tunnel will undergo six nights of timed closures for essential maintenance work.

item.title: Men arrested as cash, ketamine and cocaine seized at Holyhead addresses
item.description: Two men have been arrested on suspicion of drug supply after ketamine, cocaine and cash were seized in Holyhead.

item.title: 'Where does the council tax money go?' Gwynedd Council approves 5.17% increase
item.description: Gwynedd councillors have approved a 5.17% council tax rise for 2026/27, pushing the average band D bill just over £2,000 as the authority sets a £379.7m budget and highlights soaring demand in education and social care.

item.title: Health board to remain in special measures - Betsi Cadwaladr issues response
item.description: "Our task now is to build on this momentum and continue strengthening services for the people of North Wales.”

item.title: New Holyhead to Manchester Airport train service launched in timetable shake-up
item.description: Trains from Manchester Airport to Llandudno will now serve Holyhead instead and ferry connections to Ireland from Manchester will be enhanced.
